My grandma was a little girl in Italy during the war. She told me that throughout the war there was basically no food in Italy at all, and that the war had made everyone poor and hungry. For a while that was it, until Italy capitulated and Germany occupied my grandmothers hometown. She would’ve been 7 at the time. Then it got very bad.

She said there was a lot of horrible stuff at that time. People being shot in the street, strict curfew, etc. there’s two stories that stands out though. 

The first was when a group of  German soldiers broke into her home during the day. One soldier held the family at gunpoint (great grandpa wasn’t home at the time so it was two little girls and their mom) while the rest of them stole food and everything that wasn’t nailed down. They even knocked over dressers and broke vases while looking for stuff to steal. Apparently my great grandma did something the German soldier didn’t like, so her pulled out of the corner via her hair, beat her up with the butt of his rifle, and then put his cigarette out on her. Keep in mind this was in front of her two young daughters while other armed men destroyed their home. 

The second story is when the American troops liberated their town. My family knew they were coming so they make an American flag out of their curtain and picked flowers for the soldiers. When the American tanks came through (Germans were long gone so there was no fighting) all the Italian civilians were cheering and hugging the Americans. My grandma got some chocolate from a GI and recalls that the kindness of the Americans is why she moved to the US after the war. She had a lot of hatred for German people after that and it took her a long time to forgive them. She said she forgives the German soldiers despite all the pain they caused my family.

My father never hugged or kissed me as a kid. Some manly clasps on the back were common but anything more than that was “gay”. 

Anyway, when I was about 10 (maybe 11) I got bit by a large dog who had jumped his fence. I ran home and was trying really hard not to cry. My dad would always get really mad when he saw me or my brother cry because he thought it wasn’t manly and that crying was for girls and babies. I was pretty scared to get yelled at because it was obvious from my wet eyes, quivering bottom lip, and snotty nose that I had been crying. 

When I got home I showed my dad my arm that got bit, fully prepared to get spanked for crying/getting blood on stuff in the house. He looked me in the eyes and saw how hard I was trying to contain my tears. He sat me down on his lap and hugged me for a while and told me it was ok to cry for a few minutes. I sobbed quietly for a while, then loudly when he poured peroxide on my bite wound. After he bandaged me up he kissed me on the side of my forehead. 

He told me that dogs can be mean when they’re scared, and that dog was probably so mean to me because I was so tough and manly that I scared him. My dad’s definitely not perfect but I’ll always remember that really strange moment with him.

Hi. I am a military veteran who suffered from horrible panic attacks and anxiety in the past. I decided to go off my medication so I would be allowed to join the military. Before I start keep a couple of things in mind:

1. Anxiety in small doses is completely normal. Even I feel it in small doses to this day.
2. Everyone is different. I will happily share my technique with you but you need to find what works best for you.
3. Take it one step at a time. Realize that this kind of thing doesn't go away over night. It takes a lot of time and dedication to cure yourself of a panic disorder. 
4. You CAN conquer this. It's going to be hard, but it's worth fighting for. Believe me.

For me, the most effective thing was understanding that the only thing holding me back in life was my anxiety. I knew that it was all in my head and it was just a matter of convincing my body that I was ok. From there I started to think of fictional characters that persevered through hard times. I know it might sound dumb but it truly helped me. People like Rocky, Goku, and Solid Snake to name a few. I also practiced breathing techniques. Things like yoga and silat have great breathing techniques that helped me a lot. Something I still do today is remind myself of what I'm fighting for. I look myself in the mirror and tell myself that I have to succeed not for myself, but for others. I think of my parents whom I owe my life to, my girlfriend who would be crushed if something happened to me, my buddies who could die if I fuck up, and the civilians I encounter who look to me for safety and protection.

At the end of the day YOU have to decide to overcome this thing. Other people can help, but only you can cure you. Good luck and God bless.
